data: Skeleton entry for /fleet (PRD-012 v0.2 / Phase A scaffold). Builder + agency + first-flight per public sources. Specs and gallery TBD in later phases.
Voskhod 1 (1964-10-12) · Komarov + Feoktistov + Yegorov — first three-person crewed spaceflight; no spacesuits (fit three crew in a Vostok-derived hull)
Voskhod 2 (1965-03-18) · Belyayev + Leonov — first EVA (Leonov, 12 min); suit ballooned, required venting; manual landing in remote Urals forest

The Voskhod spacecraft was a Vostok pushed past its design, and it shows exactly what improvisation under deadline looks like. To make the one-seat capsule carry more, engineers pulled out the ejection seat — the crew's only escape — and for the first flight left out the pressure suits too; for the second they bolted on an inflatable airlock so a cosmonaut could go outside. It scored the first multi-person crew and the first spacewalk, the last two firsts the Soviet program would claim. But it had no margin left, and after the near-disaster of its second flight it was retired — a stopgap that did its narrow job and was wisely not asked to do more.

A modified Vostok refitted to carry up to three cosmonauts. Two crewed flights — Voskhod 1 (first multi-crew) and Voskhod 2 (Alexei Leonov’s first spacewalk in 1965). Pushed beyond the design margin and was retired in favour of Soyuz.
First multi-crew spaceflight — three cosmonauts in a Vostok-derived capsule
Vostok-K successor — more thrust for the heavier Voskhod capsule. Launched Voskhod 1 (1964) + Voskhod 2 (1965 Leonov EVA)
Sputnik 1 (1957). Vostok 1 — Gagarin (1961). Five hundred and forty Soyuz launches from a single pad.
First Soyuz generation; Komarov's fatal flight
Buran's atmospheric analog — equivalent of NASA's Enterprise. Four jet engines, 24 atmospheric tests 1985-88, never to orbit
Soviet shuttle; one unmanned flight, never crewed
